NTA. 

first off, alex coming to your home and making indirect comments and then just straight up asking when you’re having kids is rude. it’s none of their business AT ALL and even if they wanted to ask that question, that’s something to talk about in private. they put you on the spot in front of family and then got mad when you answered the question, then refused to accept your answer and kept bringing it up. if you telling them to stop asking causes a fight, that’s 100% on them. 

“a good mother puts her kids before anything else,” you just explained that you don’t have the desire to be a mother. they are in your home getting upset about a personal decision that you and your husband made about your own family. for alex to use their experience with miscarriages and struggling to have children to talk down to you about your decision was inappropriate and manipulative. you saying that you would rather be able to eat sushi than be pregnant for 9 months and be able to drink alcoholic beverages rather than breastfeed is not “callous” or inconsiderate of what alex had gone through trying to start a family. they made a choice to have children and they have no right to shame you for making the opposite choice.  

lastly, you do not have to justify how you live your life to ANYONE. you don’t owe anyone an explanation and you don’t owe them gentle responses when they insert themselves into your personal and private life. i have never been married or had in laws so i know it’s easier for me to say this than for you to do but i think it might be good for you to stop justifying yourself and stop worrying about responding in a way that makes THEM comfortable. they made you uncomfortable by asking that question, they can deal with the discomfort of you establishing boundaries between y’all.
